title: LETTER 11: Letter from Manager to Customer — Informing About Interest Rate Change

blocks.content: Topic: Write a formal letter from the Branch Manager to a home loan customer informing them about a change in the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) and the corresponding change in their EMI.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Official bank communication regarding interest rate changes must maintain a professional, empathetic, and clear tone.
The letter must explicitly state the revised interest rate percentage and its exact effective date.
It is mandatory to explain the impact on the customer, specifically whether the revision affects the Monthly Installment (EMI) amount or the total loan tenure.
Regulatory backing or benchmark reasons (such as RBI Monetary Policy revisions or changes in base rates/MCLR) must be cited as the cause of revision.
Clear contact information and customer support channels should be provided for further clarifications.

blocks.content: We write to inform you that in line with the recent revision in policy rates by the Reserve Bank of India, the interest rate on your loan account stands revised.
Subject: Revision in Home Loan EMI Following Change in External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR)

rows: Interest rate remains unchanged regardless of market fluctuations.
Interest rate resets periodically in alignment with benchmark updates.
No rate revision notice required during the fixed tenure.
Mandatory advance notice required informing about revised rates and EMIs.
EMI and loan tenure remain constant.
Customer may choose between increased EMI amount or extended tenure.

blocks.content: We refer to your Home Loan Account No. HL-GGN-4451237 sanctioned by our branch for Rs. 55,00,000 on 12 September 2023, linked to our External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR). In accordance with the Reserve Bank of India's mandate, your home loan is priced at EBLR plus a credit risk spread, and the EMI is subject to revision when the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee revises the Repo Rate.

We wish to inform you that with effect from 1 April 2025, the Repo Rate has been revised by the MPC. Pursuant to this revision, our EBLR has been reduced from 9.25% per annum to 9.00% per annum. Accordingly, your revised loan interest rate (EBLR + credit risk spread) stands at 8.75% per annum, down from 9.00% per annum.

As a result of this favourable revision, your monthly EMI will reduce from Rs. 49,340 to Rs. 48,615 with effect from the April 2025 billing cycle — a monthly saving of Rs. 725. If you prefer to keep your EMI unchanged and instead reduce the tenure of your loan, please write to us within 30 days of this communication, and we will make the necessary adjustments.
We take this opportunity to thank you for your continued association with Union Bank of India and assure you of our best services at all times.

items: In descriptive exams, always mention essential placeholders clearly: Loan Account Number, Revised Rate (%), Effective Date, and New EMI/Tenure details.
Ensure the subject line is concise and informative, e.g., 'Important Notice: Revision in Interest Rate on Loan Account No. XXXXXXXXX'.
Do not forget to use the proper designation in the signature block (e.g., 'Branch Manager, [Bank Name]').

blocks.content: Union Bank of India, Gurugram Branch

Examiner's Tip: Such letters demonstrate understanding of EBLR mechanism, which is a highly tested topic in bank exams. Note the logical structure: inform of rate change → explain impact on EMI → give customer an option to reduce tenure or EMI.
